analystPersona: an expert collegiate lacrosse officiating analyst and veteran referee
observationHints: Watch for contact points of stick checks (arms/chest vs. stick/hands), goalkeeper positioning and whether an attacker's foot steps on or inside the crease cylinder before the ball enters the goal, player count in offensive/defensive halves for offsides, and body checking target areas (avoiding head/neck).

rules.title: Slashing
rules.text: Slashing is a personal foul. It occurs when a player swings the crosse (stick) at an opponent's crosse or body in a reckless or uncontrolled manner, or makes contact with the opponent's body (especially head, neck, back, or legs) with their stick, other than on the gloved hand holding the crosse during a legal check.

cues.description: Look for a long, winding, or two-handed swing that misses the stick and strikes the body. A one-handed check is generally scrutinized more closely for lack of control.
Direct contact with the helmet, back, neck, or lower legs is almost always ruled a slash.

rules.sanction: 1 to 3 minute penalty (releasable, or non-releasable if flagrant).

rules.title: Slashing Exception (Gloved Hand)
rules.text: Contact with an opponent's gloved hand on the stick is not slashing, provided the contact is part of a bona fide attempt to check the opponent's crosse (stick) and does not involve excessive force.

exceptions.condition: Contact occurs on the hand that is actively holding and grasping the lacrosse stick.
exceptions.outcome: Legal stick check; no slashing penalty, provided the swing was controlled.

rules.title: Illegal Body Check
rules.text: Illegal body checking includes: checking an opponent who does not have possession of the ball (nor within 5 yards of a loose ball), checking from behind, checking an opponent above the shoulders (neck/head), or checking an opponent below the waist.

cues.description: Check if the ball is within 5 yards of the check. If the ball is further away, body contact is illegal.
Look for contact starting from the opponent's blindside or back.

rules.title: Targeting (Body Check to Head/Neck)
rules.text: No player shall initiate contact or body check an opponent to the head or neck area, or target an opponent using their own helmet/crosse. This includes any high contact with an elbow, shoulder, or head.

cues.description: Check if the defender's shoulder, elbow, or helmet makes primary contact at or above the neck line of the opponent.

rules.sanction: 3-minute non-releasable penalty; automatic ejection if flagrant.

rules.title: Cross-Check
rules.text: A player may not check an opponent with that part of the shaft of the crosse (stick) that is between the player's hands. Contact must be made with the gloved hands close together or using the hands/arms inside the frame.

cues.description: Analyze the distance between the defender's hands on the shaft. If hands are wide apart and they thrust the middle of the shaft into the opponent, it is a cross-check.

rules.title: Crease Violation
rules.text: An offensive player is not permitted to enter the opponent's goal crease (the 9-foot radius circle around the goal) at any time while the ball is in play. This includes stepping on or crossing the crease line with any part of the body or equipment.

exceptions.condition: An offensive player is pushed or checked into the crease by a defensive player.
exceptions.outcome: No crease violation, provided the attacker immediately exits the crease without interfering with the play.

cues.description: Look closely at the attacker's feet. If even a toe touches the white crease line before the ball enters the goal, the goal is disallowed.

rules.title: Goalkeeper Interference
rules.text: A player may not interfere with the goalkeeper or their stick while the goalkeeper is inside the crease area. This includes hitting the goalkeeper's stick when they are attempting to clear or pass the ball from within the crease.
rules.sanction: Technical foul. If the goalkeeper has possession, it results in a 'Play On' signal. If possession is lost or clear fails, possession is awarded to the goalie's team at the center line.

rules.title: Offside
rules.text: A team is offside when they have fewer than 4 players on their defensive half of the field (including the goalie) or fewer than 3 players on their offensive half of the field.

cues.description: Count the number of players of each team on either side of the midfield line. If a defender crosses without an attacker staying back, the team is offside.

rules.sanction: If offside team had ball: Turnover. If offside team did not have ball: 30-second technical penalty.

rules.title: Holding (Technical)
rules.text: A player may not hold an opponent or an opponent's crosse (stick) with their hands, arms, or crosse. A player may hold an opponent in possession of the ball from the front or side with closed hands, but cannot wrap or pin them.

rules.title: Pushing (Technical)
rules.text: A player may not push an opponent from behind. Pushing from the front or side is legal if the opponent has possession of the ball or is within 5 yards of a loose ball.

rules.title: Warding Off
rules.text: A player in possession of the ball may not use their free hand, arm, or any other part of their body to hold, push, or control the direction of the movement of the crosse or body of an opponent who is playing them.

cues.description: Look for the ball carrier extending their non-stick arm to actively push, grab, or sweep the defender's stick away, rather than keeping it tucked or absorbing contact.

rules.title: Conduct Foul
rules.text: A coach or player may not object to a decision, use profane language, or commit unsportsmanlike acts of low severity. This is a conduct foul.
